spec_match.rationale: Probes ProgressEvent exposure + construction + property read-back in four real realms (Window, DedicatedWorker, SharedWorker, ServiceWorker) — the cross-realm story the feature completes.

interactive.rationale: One button spawns the four realms and fills the matrix from real probes; unregister cleans up.

edge_cases.rationale: Four realms probed independently; loaded/total read-back (512/2048) proves construction, not just existence.

conformance.rationale: Shared panel executes honestly on this build.

accessibility.rationale: Matrix is a real table with headers; status output announces probe lifecycle.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment): every visible button clicked, aria-live output captured after each action, console and network clean on desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3, zero horizontal overflow, screenshots captured; conformance panel observed executing with honest fails on this pre-157 build.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, shared shell classes, no static-card pattern; verdict colors on light backgrounds.

telemetry_health.rationale: Demo telemetry loads; no unexpected console/runtime errors during the full click-through.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow and clean console at both 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800; harness-recorded state for the parent demo is ok/ok.

openQuestions.title: Confirm the stock-build matrix on Chrome 156 vs 157
openQuestions.detail: Harness cross-check: with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features Chromium 141 reports ProgressEvent exposed+constructed in all four realms (matrix run); without the flag the sibling relay worker has no ProgressEvent and says so. Both pages are honest under their respective flag states. Verify on stock Chrome 156 (expect ServiceWorker row no) and 157 (expect yes) to pin the shipped boundary.

summary: All four realm probes ran for real (512/2048 read-backs), console clean. The all-yes ServiceWorker row was obtained behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on Chromium 141; without the flag the sibling pages' worker correctly lacks ProgressEvent — consistent, flag-gated pre-157 behaviour, not a page defect.
